headline: Android toll fraud campaign used 1,235 Meta ads to push 29 Google Play apps, charging victims' phone bills
summary: A widespread Android toll fraud campaign leveraged 1,235 Meta ads and 29 Google Play apps to trick users into installing malware that silently charged their mobile accounts. CERT Polska traced the sophisticated four-stage attack chain.
details: CERT Polska analysts uncovered an Android toll fraud campaign that used 1,235 unique Meta ad records promoting 29 Google Play applications. The campaign tricked users into installing apps like "Messenger Pro" by falsely claiming PDF applications had expired.

Once installed, the malicious app exploited system-granted permissions, such as default SMS handler access, to silently deliver a four-stage encrypted payload. This payload then charged the user's mobile account without their explicit consent.

The campaign treated Google Play as a delivery mechanism, leveraging user trust in the app store. While "Messenger Pro" was reported and removed, copies on user devices remained active, and the command-and-control infrastructure continued to operate.

The visible application layer was functional, displaying a working inbox and a "Your privacy comes first" message on the permission screen. However, this facade masked the hidden code's true intent to gain extensive permissions for payment abuse.

headline: Domain search engine uncovers cybercrime infrastructure on the clear web, providing pivot points
summary: A general domain search engine, cl0q, scanned 38.5M domains and found active cybercrime operations like crypto drainers, underground marketplaces, and spamming tools, exposing their infrastructure.
details: I build cl0q, a domain search engine that has scanned 38.5 million domains, offering a free API with no tracking. The developer explored what happens when threat-intel queries are run through a general domain index instead of specialized feeds, revealing significant findings.

Top hits included infernodrainer.xyz, advertising itself as the 'best crypto drainer since 2022' with 0-day exploits and 120+ wallet support. Exogator.com, purpledrainer.club, and cryptodrainerscript.net were also found, all selling various crypto drainer scripts.

Each result came with resolved IPs and MX records, providing immediate pivot points for defenders. For instance, exogator.com sits on 5.182.209.88 and infernodrainer.xyz on 216.198.79.65, infrastructure ready for blocklists.

The search also revealed russianmarket.work, an underground marketplace selling CVV, stealer logs, and RDP, with its IPs (172.67.149.100) and metadata attached. Alongside it were breach-intel platforms, stealer-log search services, and a Turkish hacking forum (spyhackerz.org) dealing in RATs and fresh leaks.

Further findings included lurez.online and spams.tools, offering 'Spamming Tools, Office 365 Scampages, Bybit & Binance Scampages For Sale,' complete with SMTP servers and cracking utilities. These services also exposed their MX records.

While threat intelligence often relies on expensive feeds, a significant amount of attacker infrastructure resides on the clear web, using cheap domains and Cloudflare, indexed like any other site. A domain-level search engine with DNS enrichment can transform a simple hunch into actionable, pivotable infrastructure with a single query.
The cl0q search engine and its API are free to use, with no tracking or logging. All identified domains were live at the time of writing, providing valuable data for defenders.
